blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how operations like addition and multiplication can be applied in different ways? Let's explore binary operations!

blocks.markdown: In mathematics, a binary operation is a calculation that combines two elements (operands) to produce another element. Common examples include addition ($+$), subtraction ($-$), multiplication ($\times$), and division ($\div$).

blocks.title: Binary Operation
blocks.text: A binary operation on a set is a rule for combining any two elements of the set to form another element of the same set.

blocks.markdown: Consider a binary operation $*$ defined on a set $S$. For example, if $S = \{1, 2, 3\}$, and $a * b = a + b - 1$, then $1 * 2 = 1 + 2 - 1 = 2$.

blocks.title: Evaluating a Binary Operation
blocks.prompt: Given a binary operation $a * b = a^2 + b^2$ on set $S = \{1, 2, 3\}$, evaluate $2 * 3$.

steps.text: Calculate the squares and sum them.

blocks.markdown: Binary operations can also be tested for properties like commutativity. An operation $*$ is commutative if $a * b = b * a$ for all $a, b$ in the set.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: To test for commutativity, swap the operands and see if the result remains the same.
